          "text": "# Beta Mus, a Southern Pair in the Fly\n\n*This blue-white star\u2019s catalog entry hints at more than one sun\u2014but \u201cmultiple\u201d does not necessarily mean an easy split in a backyard telescope.*\n\nOn a dark March night, look south and let the sky\u2019s slow turning bring Beta Mus toward the meridian. Its name is compact; its setting is not. Musca, the Fly, is a small southern constellation, and Beta Mus lies deep in the southern sky. At declination \u221268\u00b0, it is best placed for observers south of the tropics. From far-northern latitudes, it never rises; from near the equator, it skims low above the southern horizon.\n\nThe star is marked by catalog coordinates of right ascension 12 hours 46 minutes and declination \u221268 degrees 06 minutes (J2000). Those numbers are a useful way to find it with a planetarium app or a detailed star chart. Around March, it crosses the local meridian near midnight; the exact time shifts with date and location.
